instrument.name: Policy repo rate
instrument.explainer: The repo rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends overnight to banks against government securities. The Monetary Policy Committee sets it six times a year to keep inflation close to its 4% target. Most new floating-rate retail loans are priced off it.

eras.note: Before 29 Oct 2004, RBI used "repo" for operations that absorbed liquidity. These values are kept as observations and left out of findings.
The repo rate in its international sense: the rate at which RBI lends to banks. Set by the Monetary Policy Committee since 4 Oct 2016.

transmission.benchmark: External benchmark, usually the repo rate
transmission.reset: At least once every three months
transmission.note: Most new floating-rate retail loans must be linked to an external benchmark, and most banks use the repo rate. When the rate resets, borrowers can choose a higher EMI, a longer tenure, or both.

transmission.benchmark: Bank's marginal cost of funds based lending rate
transmission.reset: On the loan's reset date, often yearly
transmission.note: Loans priced off a bank's internal MCLR follow policy moves later and usually by less.

context.label: Global financial crisis
context.description: RBI records the September 2008 global financial crisis as a sharp external shock that changed India’s monetary-policy challenge.

context.label: Tapering shock
context.description: RBI records US Federal Reserve tapering signals, capital outflows, and sharp pressure on the rupee in 2013.

context.label: Currency withdrawal
context.description: RBI recorded the 8 Nov 2016 withdrawal of legal-tender status for the ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes.

context.label: GST rollout
context.description: CBIC records the Goods and Services Tax rollout on 1 Jul 2017 as a major structural tax reform.

context.label: National lockdown
context.description: The Ministry of Home Affairs order of 24 Mar 2020 established a 21-day nationwide lockdown from 25 Mar.

context.label: War in Ukraine
context.description: RBI linked the conflict to higher global food, energy, and commodity prices and sustained inflation pressure in 2022.

context.label: Off-cycle tightening
context.description: The RBI raised the policy repo rate by 40 bps to 4.40% on 4 May 2022 amid elevated inflation pressures.

context.label: Easing cycle begins
context.description: The MPC cut the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 6.25% on 7 Feb 2025 and retained a neutral stance.
